usage: Used to describe a colour that is not bright or clear, e.g. "this blue is a bit dull."
Can come before a noun to modify a colour directly, e.g. "dark red" or "dark green."
Often used with words like "a bit" or "slightly" to sound more natural, e.g. "the colour of this shirt has become a bit dull."
Can also describe light or a place that is not bright, e.g. "the room is very dark."
